mainTopic: Penalties for a woman who remarried on a false report of her husband's death, the opinions of the lenient תנאים, and רב's ruling about a woman who remarried without the court's permission
overview: The גמרא keeps explaining the משנה about a woman who was told her husband died, remarried, and then saw her first husband return. It shows that the ban on marrying a כהן was listed only next to the new point that a בת לוי loses מעשר, and רב ששת explains that this loss is a special קנס. The בת כהן loses even תרומה דרבנן. Her sons lose כתובת בנין דיכרין, because the קנס reaches her children too. Both husbands' brothers do חליצה and not יבום, but for different reasons, one by Torah law and one by Rabbinic law. רב הונא and רבי יוחנן then disagree about which of the lenient תנאים at the end of the משנה (רבי יוסי, רבי אלעזר, רבי שמעון) agree with which, each using a קל וחומר. רב rules like the משנה's line that a woman who remarried on witnesses alone may return to her husband. רב נחמן asks why he did not openly name רבי שמעון, and this question stays unanswered. רב ששת argues the ruling was not needed and brings a ברייתא as proof, and the גמרא shows two ways the ברייתא could follow רבי שמעון, so a real dispute may remain.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious she is barred from marrying a priest?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that a בת ישראל in this case is disqualified from marrying a כהן, since this seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's statement that she becomes barred from marrying a כהן, because that seems too obvious to need saying. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She had relations with the second man while she was really still married to the first, so she is a זונה. A זונה is already forbidden to a כהן, so the משנה seems to be teaching nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious. The גמרא uses this to ask why a statement was needed at all.
A woman who had forbidden relations of a kind that bars her from marrying a כהן
The priesthood, meaning marriage to a כהן

phrases.english: It is obvious!
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה's words that a בת ישראל 'is disqualified from the priesthood.'

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens analysis of the משנה's list of disqualifications
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a בת ישראל is disqualified from כהונה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She is plainly a זונה, and a זונה is already forbidden to a כהן, so there is no new teaching here

steps.title: It was said only because of the Levite's daughter
steps.stepSummary: The real new teaching is about the בת לוי losing מעשר, and the כהונה ruling was listed alongside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא needed to teach about a Levite's daughter and the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that the כהונה ruling is obvious. It explains that the תנא needed to teach the new point about a בת לוי and מעשר, and listed the obvious case next to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every clause in a משנה has to be new. Sometimes an obvious clause is included so that the list is complete next to a clause that does teach something new. Here the new point is that a בת לוי loses her right to eat מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe given to לויים, here מעשר ראשון
It was needed by him, meaning this is the real point the תנא needed to teach

phrases.english: A Levite's daughter from the tithe
he needed to teach.
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the תנא of the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת לֵוִי מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: The obvious clause is said because of a neighboring clause that is new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each clause of the משנה must teach something new
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהונה clause is obvious, and it was listed next to the new teaching about the בת לוי and מעשר

steps.title: A ברייתא says זנות does not bar a Levite woman from מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a בת לוי loses מעשר through זנות, citing a ברייתא that says she still eats it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a Levite's daughter really disqualified from the tithe through licentiousness? But a ברייתא teaches: a Levite woman who was taken captive, or who had forbidden relations, is still given tithe and she eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the answer it just gave. A ברייתא says that a Levite woman who had forbidden relations still receives מעשר and eats it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר is not like תרומה. Forbidden relations do not take it away, so a בת לוי who is a זונה keeps her right to it. That seems to contradict the משנה's ruling that the בת לוי in our case loses מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: She was taken captive, so there is a concern that a captor had relations with her

phrases.english: And a Levite's daughter, from the tithe
is she disqualified through licentiousness?
But it was taught in a ברייתא:
A Levite woman who was taken captive,
or who had forbidden relations,
they give her tithe and she eats it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַת לֵוִי מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר מִי מִיפַּסְלָא בִּזְנוּת? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling that step 2 relied on
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the בת לוי is barred from מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows that זנות does not take away a Levite woman's right to מעשר

steps.title: רב ששת: it is a special penalty
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that losing מעשר here is a קנס from the Rabbis, not the normal law for זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is a penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that she normally would keep her מעשר. In this case, however, the Rabbis took it away from her as a penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is right that זנות by itself does not take away מעשר. This woman remarried without making sure her first husband had really died, so the Rabbis penalized her. Both sources stand: the ברייתא gives the basic law, and the משנה gives an extra penalty for this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A penalty imposed by the Rabbis

steps.whatToRemember: A בת לוי keeps מעשר even after זנות. Only in our case, where she remarried too quickly, do the Rabbis take it away as a קנס.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It is a penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: קְנָסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from the ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: The ruling is moved from basic law to a rabbinic penalty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה rules that זנות itself takes away מעשר, which contradicts the ברייתא
steps.terutzMaskana: זנות does not take away מעשר. Here she loses it because of a קנס

steps.title: A priest's daughter is barred even from תרומה דרבנן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's ruling about the בת כהן means that she is barred even from תרומה דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a priest's daughter is disqualified from תרומה. This means even תרומה from rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה and explains what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As a זונה she is obviously barred from Torah-level תרומה. So the new point of the clause must be that she is barred even from תרומה דרבנן, which is usually treated more leniently. This is the Rabbis being strict with her.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to כהנים
תרומה that is required only by rabbinic law

phrases.english: A priest's daughter, from teruma.
Even from rabbinic teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת כֹּהֵן מִן הַתְּרוּמָה. אֲפִילּוּ בִּתְרוּמָה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בת כהן in this case is barred even from תרומה דרבנן

steps.title: What כתובה could the heirs inherit?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כתובה the heirs could inherit, since the משנה already said she gets no כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: neither the heirs of this man nor the heirs of that man inherit her כתובה. But what is the כתובה doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about heirs not inheriting her כתובה and asks why this was said. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already ruled that she has no כתובה from either man. If there is no כתובה, it seems pointless to say that heirs do not inherit it.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract and the payment it promises
What is it doing here? What purpose does it serve?

phrases.english: And neither the heirs of this one
nor the heirs of that one
inherit her marriage contract, etc.
A marriage contract, what is it doing here!
phrases.notes: Earlier the משנה said she has no כתובה at all, so the question is what the heirs could possibly inherit.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתוּבָּה מַאי עֲבִידְתַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's mention of heirs inheriting her כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: She has no כתובה, so there is nothing for the heirs to inherit

steps.title: רב פפא: it means the sons' כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה means כתובת בנין דיכרין, the sons' right to inherit their mother's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It means the כתובה of the male sons.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the משנה is talking about a different right, the sons' כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a woman's sons inherit her כתובה amount from their father's estate, on top of their regular share with their brothers. The משנה teaches that her sons lose even this extra right.

keyTerms.meaning: The condition in the כתובה that her male sons inherit her כתובה amount

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's word 'heirs' points to כתובת בנין דיכרין. Her sons lose even this extra right, along with her own כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this case with her own כתובה, which she already lost. This is a separate right that belongs to her sons.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The marriage contract of the male sons.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּתוּבַּת בְּנִין דִּיכְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what כתובה is meant
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains which כתובה the משנה means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Her כתובה' means her own payment, which she already lost
steps.terutzMaskana: It means כתובת בנין דיכרין, which her sons also lose

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה's ruling about the sons' inheritance of the כתובה is too obvious to need saying.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's reading from step 7. If she gets no כתובה at all, then of course her sons can't inherit it, so why would the משנה bother to say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said she has no כתובה. The right of כתובת בנין דיכרין comes from the כתובה, so taking away the כתובה should take this away too. The גמרא is asking what new thing this line teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why does it need to be said?
The sons' right to inherit their mother's כתובה

phrases.english: This is obvious!
phrases.notes: Since the משנה already said she gets no כתובה, the sons' share in it should be gone too.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רב פפא's reading of the משנה gives the משנה anything new to teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's ruling that heirs do not inherit her כתובה, as explained by רב פפא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If there is no כתובה at all, the sons' inheritance right that comes from it is gone automatically, so saying it adds nothing.

steps.title: We might have thought the penalty is only on her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה needed to say this, because we might have thought the Rabbis penalized only the woman, not her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: she herself did something forbidden, so the Rabbis penalized her. But her children did nothing wrong, so the Rabbis did not penalize them. So the משנה teaches us that the penalty reaches them too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the line is not obvious. Without it, we could have thought the children keep their right to inherit the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing the כתובה is a קנס, a penalty for what she did. A penalty normally falls on the one who acted, so we might have thought the innocent sons are not affected. The משנה teaches that the whole כתובה is cancelled, including the sons' rights that come from it.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (introduces a mistaken assumption)
So it teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: The Rabbis' קנס on the כתובה cancels it completely, even the part her innocent sons would inherit.

phrases.english: You might have said:
regarding her herself, who did something forbidden
the Rabbis penalized her,
but her children the Rabbis did not penalize
so it teaches us that they did.
phrases.notes: The משנה needed to spell this out so we would know the sons lose out too.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by showing the line teaches something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the ruling is needed to rule out a reasonable mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קנס falls only on the woman who sinned, so her sons still inherit the כתובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קנס cancels the whole כתובה, so her sons do not inherit it either.

steps.title: Why both brothers do חליצה but not יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and explains what is Torah law and what is Rabbinic law for each husband's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the brother of this husband and the brother of that husband do חליצה and not יבום. The first husband's brother does חליצה by Torah law, and is kept from יבום by Rabbinic law. The second husband's brother does חליצה only by Rabbinic law, and he may not do יבום, by Torah law or by Rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. It explains the reason behind each part of the ruling for the two brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her marriage to the first husband is real, so his brother truly owes her יבום or חליצה by Torah law. The Rabbis blocked יבום as part of her קנס. Her marriage to the second man was a mistake and not a real marriage, so his brother owes nothing by Torah law, and יבום is not allowed at all. The Rabbis still required חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a childless widow from her brother-in-law
Levirate marriage: the brother-in-law marries the childless widow

steps.confusionAlert: The two brothers do the same actions, חליצה and no יבום, for opposite reasons. For the first brother, the חליצה is Torah law and the ban on יבום is Rabbinic. For the second brother, the חליצה is Rabbinic, and יבום is forbidden on every level.

phrases.aramaic: אָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה וְאָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה
phrases.english: The brother of this one and the brother of that one
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה: the brother of the first husband and the brother of the second husband.

phrases.english: do חליצה and do not do יבום.
The brother of the first husband does חליצה because of Torah law,
and does not do יבום because of Rabbinic law.
The brother of the second husband does חליצה because of Rabbinic law,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא מְיַיבֵּם — לָא מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא וְלָא מִדְּרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: and does not do יבום, by neither Torah law nor Rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה וְאָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה חוֹלְצִין וְלֹא מְיַיבְּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First husband's brother: חליצה by Torah law, no יבום by Rabbinic law. Second husband's brother: חליצה by Rabbinic law, no יבום on any level.

steps.title: The later תנאים agree with the earlier ones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי's opinion in the משנה, and רב הונא gives a rule for how the later תנאים in the משנה relate to the earlier ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יוסי says her כתובה is a claim on her husband's property, and so on. רב הונא said: the later ones agree with the earlier ones, but the earlier ones do not agree with the later ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reaches the end of the משנה, where several תנאים make the penalties lighter. רב הונא states a rule about how their opinions fit together, and the גמרא explains it in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each later תנא in the משנה holds the earlier תנא's leniency and goes further. The earlier תנא does not hold the later one's extra leniency. This sets up the example the גמרא gives next.

keyTerms.meaning: The later ones (the תנאים quoted later in the משנה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Her כתובה is a claim on her husband's property, and so on.
phrases.notes: He means her first husband. The "and so on" points to the rest of the משנה, where רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון also speak.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The later ones agree with the earlier ones,
but the earlier ones do not agree with the later ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בָּתְרָאֵי מוֹדוּ לְקַמָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the last section of the משנה, the lenient opinions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this משנה, each later תנא agrees with the earlier one's leniency, but not the other way around.

steps.title: Why רבי שמעון agrees with רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains, using a קל וחומר, why רבי שמעון holds רבי אלעזר's leniency about money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון agrees with רבי אלעזר. If he does not penalize her about relations, which is the main prohibition, then all the more so he does not penalize her about her found objects and her earnings, which are only money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first half of the example of רב הונא's rule. It shows why the later תנא, רבי שמעון, agrees with the earlier one, רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that relations with the first husband's brother still count, so he does not apply the קנס even to the serious matter of the prohibition itself. If he is lenient there, he will surely be lenient on the money matters where רבי אלעזר was lenient. So רבי שמעון agrees that the first husband gets her found objects and earnings.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon agrees with Rabbi Elazar:
for if regarding relations, which is the main prohibition,
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי שמעון's ruling in the משנה that relations with the first husband's brother still count.

phrases.english: he does not penalize,
then all the more so her found objects and her earnings,
which are only money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the first half of רב הונא's rule: the later תנא agrees with the earlier one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון agrees with רבי אלעזר through a קל וחומר: if there is no קנס on relations, surely there is none on money.

steps.title: Why רבי אלעזר does not agree with רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר is lenient only on money matters but keeps the קנס on relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר does not agree with רבי שמעון. Her found objects and earnings are only money, so there he does not penalize. But relations are a prohibition, so there he does penalize.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the example of רב הונא's rule. It shows why the earlier תנא, רבי אלעזר, does not accept the later one's bigger leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר only works in one direction. Being lenient on money does not mean being lenient on a real prohibition, so רבי אלעזר keeps the קנס on relations. This finishes explaining רב הונא's rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The two opinions go up a ladder. רבי אלעזר is lenient only on money. רבי שמעון is lenient even on relations, so he is surely lenient on money too. The later תנא agrees with the earlier one, but not the other way around.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: But Rabbi Elazar does not agree with Rabbi Shimon:
her found objects and her earnings, which are only money,
there he does not penalize,
but relations, which are a prohibition,
there he does penalize.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the second half of רב הונא's rule: the earlier תנא does not agree with the later one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר removes the קנס only for money matters and keeps it for relations, so he does not hold רבי שמעון's leniency.

steps.title: Both later תנאים agree with רבי יוסי about the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: Still following רב הונא, the גמרא shows that רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר both accept רבי יוסי's leniency on the כתובה, using a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them agree with רבי יוסי. If the Rabbis did not penalize her in the things that apply while she still lives with her husband, then surely they did not penalize her in the כתובה, which is meant for her to take when she leaves the marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב הונא's rule. Both later תנאים also agree with the first one, רבי יוסי, and the גמרא explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Found objects and earnings belong to her husband while she still lives with him as his wife. If the Rabbis were lenient there, while she is fully treated as his wife, then they would surely be lenient with the כתובה, which she only collects when the marriage ends. So the later תנאים have a קל וחומר for agreeing with רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: She lives under him (as his wife, under his authority)
To take and leave (the כתובה is collected when she leaves the marriage)

phrases.english: And both of them agree with Rabbi Yosei:
phrases.notes: "Both" means רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר, the two תנאים who come after רבי יוסי in the משנה.

phrases.english: these things, which apply while she lives under him,
phrases.notes: He means her found objects and earnings, which are רבי אלעזר's leniencies.

phrases.english: they did not penalize,
and all the more so the marriage contract,
which stands for taking and leaving.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ מוֹדוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב הונא's rule by showing that both later תנאים agree with the first תנא, רבי יוסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רב הונא, רבי שמעון and רבי אלעזר also hold that she does not lose her כתובה, by a קל וחומר from the things that apply while she lives with her husband.

steps.title: רבי יוסי does not agree with the later leniencies
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי, the first תנא, does not accept the later leniencies. He holds that only the כתובה was not penalized, but the things that apply while she lives with her husband were penalized.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוסי does not agree with them. Only the כתובה, which she takes when she leaves, was not penalized. But the things that apply while she lives with him were penalized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other half of רב הונא's rule. The first תנא does not agree with the ones after him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי reverses the logic. To him the כתובה only matters at the end of the marriage, so there is less reason to penalize it. But while she still lives under her husband, the Rabbis wanted the penalty to be felt. So for him, the earlier case is easier to be lenient about than the later cases.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only this that they did not penalize

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yosei does not agree with them:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתוּבָּה דִּלְמִשְׁקַל וּמִיפַּק — הוּא דְּלָא קָנֵיס,
phrases.english: the marriage contract, which is for taking and leaving, is what they did not penalize,
but these things, which apply while she lives under him, they did penalize.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא מוֹדֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse side: the first תנא does not agree with the leniencies of the later ones.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רב הונא, רבי יוסי keeps the penalty on found objects and earnings. He is lenient only on the כתובה.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: each later תנא accepts the earlier leniencies by a קל וחומר, but the earlier תנאים do not accept the later ones.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reverses the rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the opposite of רב הונא: the earlier תנאים agree with the later ones, but the later ones do not agree with the earlier ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the earlier ones agree with the later ones, but the later ones do not agree with the earlier ones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion, רבי יוחנן's. He reads the agreement between the תנאים in the reverse direction from רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the leniencies build up as you go down the משנה. רבי יוחנן says they build up as you go up: רבי יוסי, the first, accepts everything the later ones say, and the later ones are narrower. The next steps show the reasoning for each pair.

keyTerms.meaning: The earlier ones (the first תנאים in the משנה)
The later ones (the last תנאים in the משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. רב הונא: the later agree with the earlier. רבי יוחנן: the earlier agree with the later.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The earlier ones agree with the later ones,
the later ones do not agree with the earlier ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קַמָּאֵי מוֹדוּ לְבָתְרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens an alternative approach that directly opposes רב הונא's rule from step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earlier תנאים in the משנה accept the later תנאים' leniencies, but not the other way around.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees with רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי יוחנן, רבי יוסי agrees with רבי אלעזר. If the כתובה, which goes from husband to wife, was not penalized, surely her found objects and earnings, which go from wife to husband, were not penalized.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי agrees with רבי אלעזר. The כתובה, which goes from his property to her, was not penalized. So surely her found objects and earnings, which go from her to him, were not penalized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי יוחנן's rule works with the first pair: רבי יוסי accepts רבי אלעזר's leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the measure is the direction of the money. If the Rabbis let her collect the כתובה, taking money out of his pocket, they would surely let him keep what comes from her to him. The husband loses nothing he would have had anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: From his to hers (money going from him to her)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei agrees with Rabbi Elazar:
the marriage contract, which goes from his to hers, they did not penalize,
all the more so her found objects and her earnings,
which go from hers to his.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's rule to the first pair, רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יוחנן, רבי יוסי also lets the husband keep her found objects and earnings, by a קל וחומר from the כתובה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר does not agree about the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר does not accept רבי יוסי's leniency. He holds that only what goes from her to him was not penalized, but the כתובה, which goes from him to her, was penalized.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי אלעזר does not agree with him. Only her found objects and earnings, which go from her to him, were not penalized. But the כתובה, which goes from him to her, was penalized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the other side of רבי יוחנן's rule. The later תנא, רבי אלעזר, does not agree with the earlier one, רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר uses the same direction of money, but he does not turn it into a קל וחומר. Not penalizing her, when that only means the husband keeps getting what he is owed, is easy. Making the husband pay her a כתובה is a bigger step, so he keeps that penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: From hers to his (money going from her to him)

phrases.english: But Rabbi Elazar does not agree with him:
her found objects and her earnings,
it is these, which go from hers to his, that they did not penalize,
but the marriage contract, which goes from his to hers, they did penalize.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לָא מוֹדֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse side for the first pair: the later תנא does not accept the earlier one's leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר holds that she loses her כתובה.

steps.title: Both earlier תנאים agree with רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: Following רבי יוחנן, רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר both agree with רבי שמעון's leniency about the brother's relations. If things during the husband's lifetime were not penalized, surely relations after his death were not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them agree with רבי שמעון. If these things, which are during his lifetime, were not penalized, then relations after death were surely not penalized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies רבי יוחנן's rule to the last תנא. Both earlier תנאים accept רבי שמעון's leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the measure is time: during the husband's life or after his death. The money matters, the כתובה and her earnings, apply while the first husband is alive. If the Rabbis were lenient even then, surely they were lenient about the יבם's relations, which happen only after the husband has died.

keyTerms.meaning: Relations (here, the יבם's relations with her)

phrases.english: And both of them agree with Rabbi Shimon:
phrases.notes: This time "both" means רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר, the two earlier תנאים.

phrases.english: if these things, which are during his lifetime, they did not penalize,
phrases.notes: "These" are the money matters: the כתובה and her found objects and earnings.

phrases.aramaic: בִּיאָה דִּלְאַחַר מִיתָה — לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן.
phrases.english: then relations, which are after death, is it not all the more so?
phrases.notes: He means the husband's brother's relations or חליצה after the first husband dies, which רבי שמעון said still count.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ מוֹדוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's rule to the last תנא, רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יוחנן, רבי יוסי and רבי אלעזר also hold that the יבם's relations with her still work, by a קל וחומר from the money matters.

steps.title: רבי שמעון does not agree with the money leniencies
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון does not accept the earlier leniencies. Only relations after death were not penalized, but the money matters during the husband's lifetime were penalized.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי שמעון does not agree with them. Only relations after death were not penalized. But these things during his lifetime were penalized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי יוחנן's approach. The last תנא, רבי שמעון, does not agree with the earlier ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון treats after death as the easier place to be lenient. Things that apply during the husband's lifetime are the ones the Rabbis penalized. So he keeps the penalties on money during the husband's life and is lenient only on the יבם's relations. This is the opposite of what רב הונא said about רבי שמעון in step 12.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the earlier תנאים accept every later leniency by a קל וחומר, but each later תנא stays narrow. So רבי יוסי, the first, is the most lenient, and רבי שמעון, the last, is lenient only on relations after death.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Shimon does not agree with them:

phrases.aramaic: בִּיאָה הוּא דִּלְאַחַר מִיתָה לָא קָנֵיס,
phrases.english: it is relations, which are after death, that they did not penalize,
but these things, which are during his lifetime, they did penalize.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא מוֹדֵי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reverse side for רבי שמעון and closes רבי יוחנן's approach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under רבי יוחנן, רבי שמעון keeps all the money penalties and is lenient only on the יבם's relations after the husband's death.

steps.title: רב rules like the line about marrying without permission
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about a woman who remarried without the court's permission, and רב הונא reports in the name of רב that this is the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If she married without permission...' רב הונא said in the name of רב: That is the הלכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a new line of the משנה and brings רב's ruling that we follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a woman who remarried on the word of witnesses, without asking the בית דין, may go back to her first husband when he turns up. רב says this is the final הלכה. The next steps will ask why רב worded it this way, and whether he needed to say it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Without permission, meaning without the בית דין allowing it
This is the הלכה; this is how we rule

phrases.english: 'If she married without permission, etc.'
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. 'Without permission' means the בית דין never allowed her to remarry. She relied on witnesses alone.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rav said:
This is the halakha.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אֲמַר רַב: הָכִי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of which תנאים agree with each other and goes back to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows the משנה: a woman who remarried without the court's permission may return to her first husband.

steps.title: Why not say plainly that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא: why hide the ruling? If you hold like רבי שמעון, just say 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to him: Why are you sneaking it in? If you hold like רבי שמעון, say 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון,' since your ruling goes according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks the way the ruling was worded. He says it is really רבי שמעון's view and should be named as such.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'this is the הלכה' about one line of the משנה hides whose opinion it is. רב נחמן points out that this line matches רבי שמעון. So the clear way to rule is to name רבי שמעון directly.

keyTerms.meaning: To 'steal in'; to slip something in quietly instead of saying it openly
You hold; that is your opinion

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to him:
Why do you steal it in?
phrases.notes: He means: why say it in a hidden, roundabout way instead of saying it openly?

phrases.english: If you hold like Rabbi Shimon,
say: The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,
since your ruling goes according to Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּנָּבָא גַּנּוֹבֵי לְמָה לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רב's ruling from step 21.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling matches רבי שמעון's view, so it should be stated openly as 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון.'

steps.title: Even so, he could have said 'like רבי שמעון in the last case'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן blocks a possible answer. Maybe רב did not want people to think he agrees with רבי שמעון in the first case too. Then he should have said 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the last case.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: if I say 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון,' it sounds like I agree with him even in the first case. Then say: 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the last case!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן guesses what רב הונא might answer and knocks it down ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A possible defense: naming רבי שמעון would wrongly suggest that we follow him in every case, including the first one. רב נחמן answers that this is easy to fix: limit it to the last case. So the vague wording still has no good reason.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; it brings up a possible answer in order to reject it

phrases.english: And if you will say:
If I say: The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon,
it would mean even in the first case,
phrases.notes: The first case is the woman who remarried based on just one witness. There we do not follow רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: then say: The halakha follows Rabbi Shimon in the last case!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: אִי אָמֵינָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of step 22 by ruling out a likely answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible defense of רב's vague wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even if naming רבי שמעון might mislead, רב could simply have limited it to the last case, so there is still no reason for vague wording.

steps.title: The question is left standing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רב נחמן's question has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this exchange by saying the question stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' here means we have no good answer for why רב worded it this way. It does not cancel the ruling itself. It only leaves the wording unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question stays without an answer

steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' does not mean רב's ruling is thrown out. Only the question about his wording is left open; the ruling itself still stands.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב נחמן's challenge without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no explanation for why רב did not openly say 'the הלכה follows רבי שמעון in the last case.'

steps.title: רב ששת: רב said this while half asleep
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says that רב must have said this ruling while dozing off, meaning it was not carefully thought through.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: I say that רב said this teaching while he was dozing and lying down.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת opens a new attack on רב's ruling. He says it was said carelessly, and the next step explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a sharp way of saying the ruling was not needed. רב ששת is setting up his reason, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Dozing and lying down; half asleep

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: I say,
when he was dozing and lying down
Rav said this teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: אָמֵינָא, כִּי נָיֵים וְשָׁכֵיב רַב אַמְרַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new and different criticism of רב's ruling from step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling was said without careful thought.

steps.title: No one disagrees, because she was like a woman forced
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains: saying 'the הלכה is...' implies that someone disagrees. But here no one could disagree, since she had no choice and is like a woman who was forced.
steps.simpleTranslation: Saying 'it is the הלכה' implies that others disagree. But what could she have done? She was forced.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives his reason: a ruling of 'הלכה' is only needed when there is a dispute, and here there is none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses told her that her husband had died, so she had every reason to remarry. That makes her like an אנוסה, a woman forced, who may stay with her husband. Since everyone must agree, רב's ruling was not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: She was forced; she had no choice

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches a general rule of the גמרא: the words 'the הלכה is' are only used when there is a real disagreement.

phrases.english: Saying 'halakha' implies that others disagree,
but what should she have done?
She was forced!
phrases.notes: Witnesses said her husband was dead, so marrying again was not her fault. It is as if it was forced on her.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲלָכָה מִכְּלָל דִּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רב ששת's claim in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling was not needed, because no one disputes it
steps.raayaSupportSource: Logic: a woman who relied on witnesses is like an אנוסה, so no one could forbid her to her husband

steps.title: A ברייתא: marrying on witnesses' word does not even need a גט
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds a ברייתא: no forbidden union needs a גט, except a married woman who remarried by order of the בית דין. So if she married based on witnesses alone, no גט is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא: None of the forbidden unions in the Torah need a גט from him, except a married woman who remarried by order of the בית דין. So only if she married by the בית דין does she need a גט; if she married based on witnesses, she does not need a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a ברייתא to back up his point, and the גמרא draws a lesson from its exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a marriage the בית דין allowed looks serious enough to need a גט. A marriage based on witnesses alone does not even need a גט, so it barely counts at all. That fits with her being allowed back to her first husband without any debate.

keyTerms.meaning: By order or permission of the בית דין
Based on the word of witnesses alone

steps.whatToRemember: רב said a woman who remarried without the בית דין's permission may go back to her first husband. רב נחמן's question on how רב worded this stays unanswered. רב ששת says the ruling was not needed, since she is like a woman forced, and he brings a ברייתא as support. The next steps test whether that ברייתא really proves no one disagrees.

phrases.english: And it was further taught:
All forbidden unions in the Torah
do not need a bill of divorce from him,
except for a married woman
who remarried by order of the court.

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין הוּא דְּבָעֲיָא גִּיטָּא,
phrases.english: Only by order of the court does she need a bill of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי עֵדִים לָא בָּעֲיָא גִּיטָּא.
phrases.english: but based on witnesses she does not need a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד תַּנְיָא: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה אֵין צְרִיכוֹת הֵימֶנּוּ גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a written source to back up רב ששת's reasoning in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: A woman who remarried based on witnesses alone was not truly in a serious second marriage, so her return to her first husband is obvious
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that requires a גט only when she remarried by order of the בית דין

steps.title: Can the ברייתא follow רבי שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who taught רב ששת's ברייתא. It cannot be רבי שמעון, because he holds she never needs a גט, even if she remarried by order of the בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי שמעון, does he require a גט when she remarried by order of the בית דין? But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון says: if the בית דין acted on their own ruling, it is like a deliberate act of a man with a woman. If she remarried based on witnesses, it is like an accidental act. In both cases she does not need a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who taught the ברייתא from step 27. It shows that רבי שמעון cannot be the author, because elsewhere he says she never needs a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from step 27 says that when she remarried by order of the בית דין, she needs a גט. But another ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון comparing both cases to forbidden relations, one deliberate and one accidental. Neither kind of relationship ever needs a גט, so for רבי שמעון she would never need one.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? (who taught this teaching)
A ruling or instruction of the בית דין
This one and that one; both cases

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different ברייתות here. The first is רב ששת's ברייתא from step 27, which says she needs a גט if she remarried by the בית דין. The second is a new ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון, which seems to say she never needs a גט.

phrases.english: Who is [the author]?
phrases.notes: He means the ברייתא רב ששת just quoted in step 27.

phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: עַל פִּי בֵּית דִּין מִי בָּעֲיָא גֵּט?
phrases.english: does she need a get when it was by the court?
But isn't it taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
If the court acted on their own ruling,
it is like a deliberate act of a man with a woman.
If it was based on witnesses,
it is like an accidental act of a man with a woman.
In both cases she does not need a get.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִילֵימָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions who wrote the ברייתא that רב ששת brought as proof.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רב ששת's ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון holds that she needs no גט even when she remarried by the בית דין, but the ברייתא says she does need one.

steps.title: Suggestion: the ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא must follow the רבנן, not רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it the view of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא is the view of the רבנן. That would show everyone agrees in the witnesses case, which supports רב ששת. The next step pushes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes רב ששת's proof. If the ברייתא is the רבנן's, then even the רבנן agree that a woman who remarried based on witnesses is treated leniently. So no one disagrees, and רב's 'this is the הלכה' was not needed. The next step pushes back by saying the ברייתא could be רבי שמעון's after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority who disagree with רבי שמעון

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 28: the ברייתא is the רבנן's, so the רבנן agree and רב's ruling settles no real dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the author of the ברייתא?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A suggestion that the author is the רבנן.

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון, read his words differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ברייתא really is רבי שמעון's. His words should be read as being about the man's intent to marry. By the בית דין he meant marriage, so she needs a גט. By witnesses he did not, so she needs no גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is רבי שמעון, and explain it like this: רבי שמעון says, if the בית דין acted on their own ruling, it is as if the man intended marriage with the woman, and she needs a גט. If it was based on witnesses, it is as if he did not intend marriage, and she does not need a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the idea that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון. It does this by changing how we read his statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, רבי שמעון seemed to say 'deliberate' versus 'accidental,' and neither one needs a גט. Now we read him as saying 'with intent to marry' versus 'without intent to marry,' which matches רב ששת's ברייתא. So the ברייתא can be רבי שמעון's, and there is no proof that the רבנן agree. A real dispute may exist, so רב's ruling may have been needed after all.

phrases.english: Really, it is Rabbi Shimon,
and explain it like this:
Rabbi Shimon says:
If the court acted on their own ruling,
it is like a man's intent [to marry] a woman, [and she needs a get].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets, "and she needs a גט," are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: If it was based on witnesses,

phrases.aramaic: כְּשֶׁלֹּא בְּכַוּוֹנַת אִישׁ בְּאִשָּׁה [וְלֹא בָּעֲיָא גֵּט].
phrases.english: it is like a man without intent [to marry] a woman, [and she does not need a get].

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, וְתָרֵיץ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 29 by answering the problem of step 28. This undoes רב ששת's proof that רב's ruling was not needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the conflicting source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון said 'deliberate' versus 'accidental,' so she never needs a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון said 'with intent to marry' versus 'without it,' so she needs a גט when she remarried by the בית דין.

steps.title: רב אשי: רבי שמעון was talking about the first husband
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says רבי שמעון's statement is not about a גט at all. It is about whether she becomes forbidden to her first husband. By the בית דין she is forbidden to him; by witnesses she is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: he taught this about the prohibition, and this is what he meant. If the בית דין acted on their own ruling, it is like a deliberate act of a man with a woman, and she is forbidden to her husband. If it was based on witnesses, it is like an accidental act, and she is not forbidden to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different answer. He keeps רבי שמעון's original words but says they are about a different question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's 'deliberate' and 'accidental' tell us whether she is forbidden to her first husband, like a woman who sinned on purpose or by accident. He never said she does not need a גט. So nothing stops רב ששת's ברייתא, which requires a גט when she remarried by the בית דין, from following רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: About the matter of the prohibition
She becomes forbidden to her husband

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to fit the ברייתא to רבי שמעון. The first rereads 'deliberate' and 'accidental' as 'with or without intent to marry.' רב אשי says the words are about whether she is forbidden to her first husband, not about a גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both answers let the ברייתא be רבי שמעון's view. Then there is no proof that the רבנן agree, so רב ששת's claim that no one disputes רב's ruling is not proven.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said,
he taught it about the prohibition,
phrases.notes: He means whether she becomes forbidden to her first husband, not whether she needs a גט.

phrases.english: and this is what he said:
If the court acted on their own ruling,
it is like a deliberate act of a man with a woman,
and she is forbidden to her husband.
If it was based on witnesses,
it is like an accidental act of a man with a woman,
and she is not forbidden to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר, לְעִנְיַן אִיסּוּרָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the problem of step 28, instead of the rereading in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the subject of the conflicting source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's 'deliberate' and 'accidental' were about whether she needs a גט.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are about whether she is forbidden to her first husband, so they say nothing against needing a גט.
